title: Symplectic Weil Representation over a Finite Field
body_html:
Symplectic Weil Representation over a Finite Field

Let $(E,j)$ be a nondegenerate symplectic space of dimension $2\ell$ over a finite field $k$ of odd order, let $H(E,j)$ be its Heisenberg group, and let $S(E,j)$ be its symplectic group. For every nontrivial central character $\xi$ of $H(E,j)$, there is a distinguished representation class $$ W_\xi^{E,j} $$ of $S(E,j)$, called the Weil representation associated to $\xi$, characterized by the property that any realization of the Heisenberg representation $\eta_\xi^{E,j}$ extends to $S(E,j)H(E,j)$ and restricts to $W_\xi^{E,j}$ on $S(E,j)$.

If $E=E^+ \oplus E^-$ is a Witt decomposition and $G$ is the stabilizer of both $E^+$ and $E^-$ in $S(E,j)$, then the restriction of $W_\xi^{E,j}$ to $G$ is $$ \chi_G \otimes W^G, $$ where $\chi_G$ is the nontrivial real one-dimensional character of $G$ and $W^G$ is the corresponding general linear Weil representation.
